AML, OFAC & Beneficial Ownership — Current Status and File Protocol

Current through September 17, 2026. Federal reporting rules moved sharply; sanctions screening and source-of-funds discipline did not disappear with them.

What is actually in force today

CTA domestic BOIEnded. FinCEN’s final rule became effective August 14, 2026: U.S. companies and U.S. persons are exempt. Certain foreign entities registered in the U.S. still report foreign beneficial owners.
Residential Real Estate RuleNo current filing duty. A federal district court vacated the rule on March 19, 2026. FinCEN and DOJ appealed, but FinCEN says the rule has no legal effect while that order remains in force.
OFAC sanctionsStill live. U.S. persons cannot transact with blocked persons or property interests absent authorization. Screening must reach ownership, not just the entity’s name.
Bank / title diligenceStill real. A client’s lack of a direct broker filing does not stop lenders, banks, title agents or insurers from demanding ownership and source-of-funds evidence.
Do not use an old checklist. A 2024 memo saying every domestic LLC must file BOI is obsolete. A 2025 memo saying the Real Estate Report is mandatory is also obsolete after the 2026 vacatur. Preserve the source and date for the status relied on.
Treasury — August 11, 2026 BOI final rule announcement FinCEN — current BOI FAQs FinCEN — Residential Real Estate Rule FAQ / vacatur

Screen the deal, not only the buyer name

Resolve the natural people

Collect formation jurisdiction, registered name, managers, direct and indirect owners, control persons, signers and anyone providing purchase funds. Get IDs and an ownership chart where entities stack.

Screen every relevant name

Search buyer, seller, lender, guarantor, principals, signers and funding parties. Save the result date, search terms and disposition of possible matches.

Apply OFAC’s 50 Percent Rule

An entity owned directly or indirectly 50% or more in the aggregate by one or more blocked persons is itself blocked even if its name is absent from the SDN list.

Understand the money

Bank, country, account holder, funding path, third-party wires, private loans and cryptocurrency conversion. A clean name does not explain an unexplained payment.

Escalate; do not diagnose sanctions alone

A possible match, sanctioned-country nexus, blocked ownership issue or evasive ownership chain goes to qualified counsel and the financial institution before performance.

OFAC Sanctions List Search OFAC — 50 Percent Rule FAQs OFAC — evaluating and reporting a valid match

Loan brokerage — a separate AML question

The real-estate reporting vacatur does not suspend the separate AML-program and suspicious-activity reporting obligations for covered residential mortgage lenders and originators. Have compliance counsel classify the loan business by its actual activities; do not assume the same rule applies to a commercial-only brokerage. Record the determination, responsible officer and applicable procedures.

FinCEN FAQ C.4 — financial institutions with AML / SAR obligations

International-client intake — risk-based file

Use proportionate, consistently applied diligence—not nationality-based assumptions. Collect sensitive documents only when needed through an approved secure system with restricted access and a retention policy. Do not store IDs, bank statements, account numbers or passport details in this HTML tool or its deal notes.

  • Government ID, citizenship, residence, tax residence and U.S. visa/status if relevant to closing or financing.
  • Certified entity documents, good standing, operating agreement or equivalent, ownership chart and signing authority.
  • Source of wealth and source of transaction funds—different questions—with supporting bank, sale, income, inheritance or business records.
  • All accounts and third parties expected to send money; written explanation and documentation for any mismatch between buyer and sender.
  • OFAC search record at onboarding and refreshed before contract/LOI, before funds move and immediately before closing.
  • Foreign-investment restrictions and affidavits under Florida law checked separately; OFAC clearance is not Florida land-law clearance.

Wire instructions live here too

International wires add bank, language, time-zone and correspondent-bank friction, but the control does not change: secure delivery, independent callback, dual approval, no email-only change, immediate bank confirmation. The complete incident protocol is on E&O Coverage.

Condo Termination — Association-Level Acquisition Playbook

A sourcing strategy for aging South Florida condominiums where the land or redevelopment value may exceed the value of continued fragmented ownership. This is a lawyer-led process, not a normal unit-by-unit assemblage.

The threshold that controls the sourcing thesis

80%Optional termination approval — residential association
5%Rejection / written objection can stop optional plan
14 daysPlan delivered before vote / solicitation
45 daysDivision review notice period
Do not market “80% and you own it.” For an optional residential termination, at least 80% must approve, but 5% or more can reject and stop the plan. Declaration language, mortgages, title defects, owner protections, DBPR review, appraisal and court challenges can control the outcome. Retain Chapter 718 counsel before contacting a board as a termination sponsor.

The two statutory doors

PathWhen it existsWhy it matters
Economic waste / impossibility
§718.117(2)		Necessary construction/repair cost exceeds combined post-repair fair market value, or land-use law makes operation/reconstruction to prior configuration impossible.Threshold follows the lesser declaration amendment percentage or the declaration’s termination provision, subject to the statute. Requires real engineering, valuation and land-use evidence.
Optional termination
§718.117(3)		Plan meets the statute and receives division approval; residential plan first receives at least 80% approval and less than 5% rejection.This is the classic acquisition route, but the 5% blocking threshold makes owner strategy and fair economics decisive.

Build the target list from pressure, not age alone

Inspection pressureMilestone reports, structural deterioration, unsafe-building activity, repair scope and deadlines.
Reserve pressureSIRS, waived/underfunded history, new reserve line items, special assessment and delinquency.
Insurance pressureNonrenewal, roof limits, Citizens placement, deductible burden, uncovered code upgrades.
Land-value gapLow existing FAR or units per acre versus current zoning/FLU and assembled frontage.
Ownership readinessInvestor concentration, long tenure, absentee ownership, recent bulk purchases and board posture.
Execution frictionHomestead count, mortgages above proceeds, pending litigation, commercial units, timeshares and title defects.

Best first signal: a special-assessment or inspection problem sitting on land whose residual value is materially higher than the sum of unit values plus transaction, relocation, legal, carrying and demolition costs.

Termination residual — the acquisition screen

Start withSubtractThe result
Land / redevelopment residual value supported by zoning, density, buildable SF, hard/soft costs, finance and exit assumptionsAll unit compensation + mortgage/title cures + statutory owner protections + legal/DBPR/trustee + relocation + carrying + demolition/remediation + contingencyMaximum assemblage price and sponsor margin. If the margin only works by minimizing owner rights or using wholesale/distress unit comps, it does not work.
Bulk-owner protections matter to the model. Where the statutory bulk-owner conditions apply, non-bulk owners receive at least fair market value; qualifying homestead or owner-occupied operating-business owners who are current may receive a floor tied to original purchase price; qualifying homestead owners receive the additional statutory relocation payment; and occupants may have a 12-month lease right if former units are offered to the public.

Execution sequence

Desktop screen

Declaration and amendments, unit count/mix, ownership concentration, mortgages, zoning/FLU, parcel configuration, inspection and reserve records, litigation and code.

Confidential sponsor underwriting

Development residual, acquisition waterfall, holdouts, owner-protection budget and at least two downside cases. No owner outreach until counsel validates the route.

Board / association engagement

Use counsel-approved communications. Disclose sponsor, broker and affiliated interests. Do not imply the board has approved a plan that does not exist.

Plan, appraisal and title work

Independent appraiser, termination trustee, mortgage/lien analysis, sworn bulk-owner disclosures, statutory notice and DBPR submission.

Vote, objections and closing

Track every consent, rejection, objection period, cure and recording condition. Assume litigation time and carry until the plan is effective and title vests as provided.

Primary statute

2026 F.S. 718.117 — Termination of condominium DBPR — Condominiums and Cooperatives
Deal-team requirement. Chapter 718 counsel, land-use counsel, independent appraiser, title, structural engineer, insurance adviser and tax counsel. The brokerage sources and coordinates; it does not render the statutory, appraisal or engineering opinions.
